Q-TRIAL.text: How long should the free trial be?
Q-TRIAL.context: Habits take about two weeks to stick, so a 7-day trial ends before users see the value. 30 days delays revenue with little gain in the beta data.
Q-TRIAL.if_yes: BILL-3 builds a 14-day trial this round, and the beta can measure who converts after two weeks.
Q-TRIAL.if_no: BILL-3 builds the trial you pick: 7 days ends before habits stick, 30 days delays revenue by a month.

Q-VAT.text: Which countries do we charge VAT in at launch?
Q-VAT.recommendation: Start with the EU only; add others when there are customers there.
Q-VAT.context: Stripe Tax can collect EU VAT from day one. Other countries need their own registration, which costs time before there is any revenue.

Q-SSO.text: Do we offer sign-in with Apple and Google from day one?
Q-SSO.context: Apple requires Sign in with Apple on iOS when an app offers any other social sign-in. Google adds a second consent screen and review for little gain in the beta.
Q-SSO.if_yes: AUTH-4 adds Apple sign-in now, which iOS review requires; Google waits for a later round.
Q-SSO.if_no: Both providers in one round: a second consent screen and a Google review before the beta ships.

Q-CONFLICT.text: Decide how sync conflicts are shown: silent last-write-wins or a choice for the user.

# Pebble roadmap

Where Pebble is going and why, written for people. The queue never reads this file: a task links to a plan entry
(the PL- ids below), and the plan entry points at its plan document under docs/plans/.

## 1. Where we are

Pebble 0.3 is a private beta with about 400 testers on iOS and Android. Habits, streaks and reminders work well on
one device. The testers ask for three things: an account, so a new phone does not lose their streaks; sync between
phone and tablet; and a way to pay for an app they like.

## 2. Before the public launch

### 2.1 Accounts (PL-AUTH)

Email and password first, then Sign in with Apple once the owner has decided on social sign-in. Sessions must survive
a lost phone without giving the finder a way in.

### 2.2 Sync between devices (PL-SYNC)

The most requested feature in the beta. A user's habits are the same on every device, also after a day offline.
This is the active plan.

### 2.3 Paid plans (PL-BILL)

Pebble stays free for three habits. Pebble Plus unlocks the rest, with a free trial long enough for a habit to stick.

## 3. After the launch

Home screen widgets (PL-WIDGETS) and sharing streaks with friends (PL-SOCIAL). Both wait for usage data from the
launch, so we build what people use and not what we guess.

## 4. Open and dropped

- Full offline mode (PL-OFFLINE) is open: a big effort that the owner weighs against sync.
- Data export as files (PL-EXPORT) is dropped for now: the sync API already gives users their data.

## 5. How this document is kept

Edited by hand at each milestone. It names plan ids, never task ids, so it does not go stale when the queue moves.
docs.docs/plans/auth.md:
# Accounts and sign-in

Plan entry PL-AUTH. The roadmap tells the story; this document holds the rules the auth tasks build to.

## 1. Scope and rules

Pebble gets accounts so a user keeps their habits and streaks when they change phones. Every auth task follows these
rules:

- An account is keyed on its user id (a UUID), never on the email address. The email can change.
- No password, token or email address in a log line or an error message.
- Every auth endpoint answers with the shared error shape `{ code, message }`, and the message never says whether an
  email address has an account.
- Times are stored in UTC.

## 2. Design

### 2.1 Email and password

Passwords are hashed with argon2id (64 MB memory, 3 passes). A new account confirms its email before sync turns on.
Sign-in returns an access token (15 minutes) and a refresh token.

### 2.2 Sessions and refresh tokens

One row per signed-in device in `sessions`: user id, device name, a hash of the refresh token, and the created and
last-used times. A refresh rotates the token, and the old one stops working at once. A refresh token used twice ends
every session of that user, since one of the two uses was not the user.

### 2.3 Abuse protection

- Sign-in is rate limited to 5 attempts per minute per IP address and 10 per hour per account. Over the limit the
  endpoint answers 429 with `Retry-After` and the same message as a wrong password.
- The counters live in Redis with a time to live, so nothing about a failed attempt is kept for long.
- An account locks for 15 minutes after 10 failed sign-ins in a row, and the user gets an email with a reset link.

### 2.4 Password reset

A reset link is valid for 30 minutes and works once. Using it ends every other session of the account.

### 2.5 Sign in with Apple

For the iOS app, and it waits on the owner question Q-SSO. An Apple relay address is stored like any other email.

## 3. Build order

1. AUTH-1 email and password sign-in, AUTH-2 sessions and refresh tokens.
2. AUTH-3 rate limit, AUTH-5 password reset.
3. AUTH-4 Sign in with Apple, after Q-SSO.
4. AUTH-6 review of the token storage on mobile: tokens stay in the iOS Keychain and the Android Keystore.

## 4. Decision log

- 2026-10-02: argon2id over bcrypt, since the hosting has the memory for it.
- 2026-10-20: refresh tokens rotate on every use.
- 2026-11-12: lock the account after 10 failed sign-ins (review of AUTH-2, finding M1).
docs.docs/plans/billing.md:
# Paid plans with a free trial

Plan entry PL-BILL. The rules the billing tasks build to.

## 1. Scope and rules

Pebble stays free for up to three habits. Pebble Plus unlocks unlimited habits, the full history and sync to more
than two devices.

- Stripe handles cards and payment details. Pebble never sees or stores a card number.
- Prices are stored in minor units (cents) with a currency code, never as a decimal number.
- Only a Stripe webhook changes a subscription. The app never trusts its own checkout redirect.

## 2. Design

### 2.1 Plans and prices

`plans` holds a monthly and a yearly price per currency (EUR, USD and NOK at launch). A price is never edited: a
new price is a new row, so an old invoice still shows what the user paid.

### 2.2 Checkout

Stripe Checkout opens in the system browser and returns to the app with a deep link. The app shows "Waiting for
payment" until the webhook has changed the subscription.

### 2.3 Free trial

One trial per account. Its length waits on the owner question Q-TRIAL (the recommendation is 14 days).

### 2.4 VAT and invoices

Stripe Tax collects the VAT; which countries at launch waits on Q-VAT. Invoices show the VAT on its own line.

### 2.5 Webhooks

Every webhook's signature is checked with the signing secret before anything in it is read. Events are stored by
event id, so an event Stripe sends twice is applied once.

## 3. Build order

1. BILL-1 plans and prices.
2. BILL-2 checkout, then BILL-5 webhook signatures.
3. BILL-3 free trial after Q-TRIAL, BILL-4 VAT after Q-VAT.

## 4. Stripe notes

- Use Stripe's own test mode and its published test cards in development, never a real card.
- The webhook events Pebble handles: checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.updated and
  customer.subscription.deleted.
docs.docs/plans/sync.md:
# Cloud sync between devices

Plan entry PL-SYNC. The rules the sync tasks build to.

## 1. Scope and rules

A user's habits, check-ins and streaks are the same on every device they sign in on, also after a day offline.

- The server is the source of truth; each device keeps a local SQLite copy.
- Every change is a row in an append-only change log. Nothing is updated in place on the server.
- Sync survives a bad mobile network: every request can be retried without doing the work twice.
- A sync response carries the signed-in user's own data and nothing else.

## 2. Design

### 2.1 Change log and cursors

`changes` holds one row per change: user id, entity, entity id, operation, payload, server time and a sequence
number. Each device keeps the last sequence number it has seen (its cursor) and asks for everything after it.

### 2.2 Client queue and retry

The client writes each local change to an outbox table first, then sends the outbox in batches of up to 200 changes.
A failed batch is retried with backoff (2, 4, 8 seconds and so on, at most 5 minutes). Every change carries a client
id, so a retried batch is applied once.

### 2.3 Conflicts

Two devices can change the same habit while offline. How the user sees that waits on the owner task Q-CONFLICT:
silent last-write-wins, or a choice for the user.

### 2.4 Status in the header

The header shows one of three states: synced, syncing, or offline with the number of changes waiting.

## 3. Protocol findings

From the investigation SYNC-1. Three approaches were compared on a test set of 50,000 check-ins:

| Approach | Data per sync | Effort | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full snapshot | 1.8 MB | Low | Too heavy on mobile data |
| CRDT per habit | 40 KB | High | More than a habit tracker needs |
| Change log with cursor | 12 KB | Medium | Chosen |

The change log also gives support the history of a habit for free, which they asked for.

## 4. Build order

1. SYNC-1 investigation, SYNC-2 change log and cursors.
2. SYNC-3 client queue with retry, SYNC-5 status in the header.
3. SYNC-4 conflict handling, after Q-CONFLICT.
